core_fields.title: Climate Resilience Assesment
core_fields.description:
Measure your impact on household resilience. Collect actionable insights and learn how farmers are experiencing climate shocks.

Why build a Climate Resilience Assessment?
The Climate Resilience Assessment is a standardised and simple methodology for measuring impacts on household resilience to climate shocks.

Finance for climate adaptation in emerging markets is 5-10x below what is needed, and the gap is widening. One barrier to financing adaption has been the absence of clear metrics – how do investors know if they’ve built resilience?

At 60dB, we believe there is a lean way to measure resilience. For the last decade, our team has continuously tested ways to get climate-conscious investors relevant, affordable, and data-driven insights. Through focusing on things that social enterprises can actually impact, we give sector leaders – from bilateral donors to country governments – the data they need.

Our past work with the UN, published here, did just that; we evaluated the preemptive measures UN agencies took to prepare the Somalians for a long drought. Our lean resilience measurement strategy focuses on measuring impact—or changes to resilience—rather than diagnosing a household’s vulnerability to shocks. By developing standardized metrics, we’ve created a tool that can be used across different households, farming communities, and non-agricultural households, providing actionable insights to better improve their climate resilience.

1. Listen to vulnerable households
Understand farmers’ lived experience of climate risks they face
2. Assess your impact
Measure your impact on how households experience climate events
3. Understand resilience behaviours
Learn about farmers’ current practices and resources and identify opportunities to improve their resilience

core_fields.title: Cadeia de Valor de Terra Comunitária - CaVaTeCo
core_fields.description:
The Community Land Value Chain (or CaVaTeCo, after the Portuguese version of the name, Cadeia de Valor de Terra Comunitária) is a suite of tools, methodologies and support services that allow local communities to formally map their collective land rights over a specific territory. Once complete, the individual farmers and households within that community can also choose to undertake a systematic land tenure regularisation process across that territory, mapping out their individual and household landholdings, as well as communally managed areas, community reserves, sacred sites and areas for development and expansion.

The platform is driven by digital data collection forms that pull together all the needed information for the formal first-time registration and recognition of both the community and the household land rights.

core_fields.title: FarmHive
core_fields.description:
FarmHive is the Social Network for Agriculture! A short overview video is here.

The web platform (www.farmhive.co) and Mobile Apps include the following basic social features for Farmers, Agronomists & Researchers:

- A Profile enables users to identify themselves, their location, and types of farming they are involved in.

- A Social Feed and Posts allow users to share updates, ask questions or report issues to others in the network.

- The Chat tool enables users to chat via text and media sharing.

- Users can Search for, Connect and Follow other users 

In addition, other features specific to the agricultural field have been developed in FarmHive:

The Forum is a digital tool for asking and answering questions about farming, with advanced filters making it easy to find or post information about specific topics.

The Library (www.farmhive.co/library) tool allows users to upload, manage and share digital resources with others. From PDF documents to photos or videos, users can keep track of their resources in one place, while making it easy for others to search for and find them using advanced filters.

The Farm Journal tool (under development) is a digital record of the farm, including cropping history and main activities, that can be easily shared with other stakeholders such as farm advisors or agronomists for providing an in-depth digital snapshot of the farm in order to accelerate knowledge sharing. Farmers may also invite others to share notes, edit or comment on their Farm Journal, and have control over who has access to it. A short video of the tool is available here.
